core_obligations: Start from the witness (proof lines 18123-18129): choose the diagram and sheaf supplied by the failure lemma and assume S' affine.
Enlarge the base to the function field (proof lines 18130-18138): let K' be the function field of S' and form the extended diagram with Y' = X' x_{S'} Spec(K') and Y over Spec(K).

Transport the nonvanishing (proof lines 18139-18147): by the invariance lemma the total direct image R(Y -> Y')_*Z/dZ is isomorphic to Z/dZ in D(Y'_etale) — here the invertibility of n on S is used — so the relative Leray spectral sequence gives R h'_* Z/dZ = R h_* Z/dZ, and the already obtained nonvanishing transfers to the new diagram whose base is affine, integral and normal with algebraically closed function field K.
proof_roadmap: Take the existing witness of the failure of BC(f, n, q) and assume the base affine.
Pass to the function field of the enlarged base and form the extended cartesian diagram.
Use invariance under field extensions to identify the two pushforwards of Z/dZ along the two closed points, transferring the nonvanishing.
difficulty_reason: The lemma refines a witness for the failure of the base change condition BC(f, n, q) so that the base becomes affine, integral and normal with algebraically closed function field (statement lines 18105-18120). The proof (proof lines 18122-18147) starts from the existing witness, passes to the function field K' of S', and transfers the nonvanishing of R^q h_* Z/dZ to the new diagram using invariance of cohomology under the extension to the separably closed function field and the relative Leray spectral sequence. H2: one base change of the witness plus one transport of the nonvanishing, written out.
